title: Growing Memory with realloc
instructions: malloc gives you a fixed chunk of memory. But what if you need MORE later? That's what realloc is for.
realloc(arr, newSize) resizes an existing block, keeping what was already in it.
It lives in <stdlib.h>, next to malloc and free.
Here we start with room for 2 numbers, then grow to 4.
Always assign the result back: arr = realloc(arr, ...); Then free it when done.
task: Fill in realloc to grow arr to hold 4 ints, so it prints 1 2 3 4 (each on a line).
hint:
Resize to 4 ints:

    arr = realloc(arr, 4 * sizeof(int));
